[[Perak FA|Perak]] | continentalcup2 = [[ASEAN Club Championship]] | continentalcup2 qualifiers = [[Pahang FA|Pahang]] | league topscorer = [[Indra Putra Mahayuddin]] (15 goals, [[Pahang FA|Pahang]]) | biggest home win = | biggest away win = | matches = 84 | total goals = 271 | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = | longest losses = | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2003 Liga Perdana 1|2003]] | nextseason = [[2005 Malaysia Super League|2005]] }} The '''2004 Liga Super''', also known as the '''Dunhill Liga Super''', was the inaugural season of the [[Liga Super]], the top-tier professional [[association football|football]] league in Malaysia.[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay04.html] 2004 Liga Super The season was held from 14 February and concluded on 14 August 2004. This league participated by 8 teams, six west teams and two east teams, Sabah and Sarawak. The [[Liga Super]] champions for 2004 was [[Pahang FA|Pahang]]. [[Pahang FA|Pahang]] dominated the season and ended up winning the title by a wide margin and this was down to their efforts in securing the services of the nation's top players prior to the start of the new season. [[Pahang FA|Pahang]]'s [[Indra Putra Mahayuddin]] was the season's top goalscorer with 15 goals. He held the record as the only local players which won the accolade until the end of [[2009 Liga Super|2009 season]]. The highest scoring match of the season was [[Perlis FA|Perlis]] 6–2 defeat of [[Kedah FA|Kedah]] on 31 July 2004. Another surprising club performance in this season was the strong finish of club side [[Public Bank F.C.|Public Bank]]. At this time, the [[Football Association of Malaysia]] were trying to promote clubs as the future of Malaysian football. ==Team changes== The following teams have changed division since the 2003 season. {{col-begin|width=auto}} {{col-break}} ===To Malaysia Super League=== '''Promoted from [[2003 Liga Perdana 2|Liga Perdana 2]]''' * [[Public Bank F.C.|Public Bank FC]] {{col-break|gap=3em}} ===From [[2003 Liga Perdana 1]]=== '''Relegated to [[2004 Malaysia Premier League|Premier League]]''' * [[Johor FC]] * [[TM F.C.|Melaka Telekom]] * [[Kelantan FA]] * [[Malacca FA]] * [[Selangor FA]] * [[Terengganu FA]] {{col-end}} ==Stadiums and locations== {{Location map+ |Malaysia |float=none |width=800 |caption=Locations of teams in the 2004 Liga Super |places= {{Location map~ |Malaysia |lat=6.136021 |long=100.371764 |label=[[Kedah FA|Kedah]] |position=bottom }} {{Location map~ |Malaysia |lat=3.814767 |long=103.323948 |label=[[Pahang FA|Pahang]] }} {{Location map~ |Malaysia |lat=4.609433 |long=101.103439 |label=[[Perak FA|Perak]] }} {{Location map~ |Malaysia |lat=5.260874 |long=100.437468 |label=[[Penang FA|Penang]] }} {{Location map~ |Malaysia |lat=6.450438 |long=100.200559 |label=[[Perlis FA|Perlis]] }} {{Location map~ |Malaysia |lat=5.5900 |long=116.0544 |label=[[Sabah F.C.
